auditlens.reply:
Yes
From an audit perspective, this practice is verifiable directly from git history. The commit history and diffs provide an unambiguous audit trail: an auditor can verify that a corpus commit precedes the red commit, that it contains at least five distinct shape families with inputs and expected outputs, and that the red commit incorporates them as test rows. Because the temporal sequence and artifact presence are committed to the repository tree, the team cannot pass an audit without creating the required pre-red commit. Auditing the substantive realism of the shape families requires domain review, but procedurally this leaves no loophole.
